title: Analyzing Palmer Penguins Data
text:
Flipper length and body mass
The following graph demonstrates the relationship between flipper lengths and body mass. The different colours and shapes depict the different species.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
adelie = penguins[penguins["species"] == "Adelie"]
chinstrap = penguins[penguins["species"] == "Chinstrap"]
gentoo = penguins[penguins["species"] == "Gentoo"]

plt.scatter(adelie["flipper_length_mm"], adelie["body_mass_g"],
color="#A8DADC", marker="o", label="Adelie")

plt.scatter(chinstrap["flipper_length_mm"], chinstrap["body_mass_g"],
color="#F4A6A6", marker="s", label="Chinstrap")

plt.scatter(gentoo["flipper_length_mm"], gentoo["body_mass_g"],
color="#CDB4DB", marker="^", label="Gentoo")

plt.xlabel("Flipper length (mm)")
plt.ylabel("Body mass (g)")
plt.legend()
plt.show()







Figure 1: Flipper length and body mass of Palmer Penguins, by species.

title: Analyzing Palmer Penguins Data
text:
Findings
Based on the graph, it is clear that flipper length tends to increase as body mass increases. In particular, Gentoo are the largest penguin species and have both the heaviest body mass and the longest flipper length.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
During our first week at orientation, I didn’t take many photos, but I did still work at my part-time job of puppy yoga.


My first few weeks of the MDS program have been a whirlwind to say the least! Orientation was a wealth of information on how to best tackle the program, where to find resources available to us, and a wonderful way to meet the people in my cohort.
On top of the beginning of MDS, I began my first ever TA position. So far, I am loving it, and I don’t want to jinx it but the balance between MDS work and grading has been good! It is nice to have another task to focus on.
I have found the process of learning git and how to submit assignments to be challenging, but very interesting. At this point, I think DSCI 551 will be the most challenging course for myself in block one, but we have quiz week next week so time will tell!
